On this page

Adjoint status ​

This page marks the current boundary of the adjoint implementation: what can be run and tested today, and which combinations are deliberately rejected. The LinRood adjoint and TM5-style inversion scaffold are implemented and covered by the core test suite, but real-data parity with TM5-4DVAR remains a validation gap.

For a first introduction, start with Learning adjoints and inversions and the executed footprint tutorial. This page is the support reference, not the starting lesson.

What is shipped ​

Forward operators (unchanged) ​

The forward transport model — advection (four schemes: UpwindScheme, SlopesScheme, PPMScheme, LinRoodPPMScheme), convection (CMFMC + TM5), implicit vertical diffusion (Beljaars–Viterbo / Holtslag–Boville Kz fields), and surface flux sources — is implemented for the runtime's supported topology/backend combinations and covered by the test suite documented in Conservation budgets.

Tape, checkpoint, and reverse pass ​

src/Adjoints/ ships a full discrete-adjoint pipeline for the cubed-sphere split-sweep path, with a separate kernel-level pipeline for LinRoodPPMScheme integrated through cs_surface_emission_footprint.

The shipped pieces, all exported through AtmosTransport.Adjoints:

SurfaceWhat it does
cs_surface_emission_footprintForward → tape → reverse pass driver for CS, returning dJ/dE_t at every surface step
cs_surface_emission_footprint_from_seedSame, but accepts an explicit final dJ/drm seed for arbitrary observation operators
cs_surface_flux_jacobianBatches layer/column objectives on one recorded tape (one reverse walk per objective), aggregates per-step footprints into named user windows
cs_surface_flux_4dvar4D-Var cost / gradient with named controls, scalar observations sampled at one step or over a time window (layer, column-mean, point samples placed in the column, and averaging-kernel columns), diagonal background; one taped run and one reverse pass per gradient, whatever the number of observations (single-sweep gradient, observation operators, averaging-kernel columns)
cs_surface_flux_4dvar_optimizeDependency-free gradient-descent driver for the above
cs_surface_flux_4dvar_solveProduction driver with optimizer choice (CSGradientDescent / CSLBFGS)

The adjoint supports the following advection schemes (full union in CSAdjointSupportedScheme):

  • UpwindScheme()

  • SlopesScheme(NoLimiter())

  • PPMScheme(NoLimiter())

  • PPMScheme(MonotoneLimiter()) and PPMScheme(CW84Limiter()) — via a stored tracer-branch tape around the base trajectory

  • LinRoodPPMScheme(5) and LinRoodPPMScheme(7), with either vertical sweep: FV3's kord = 8 profile (vertical = "fv3_kord8", the configured default, or "fv3_kord8_signed") or upwind (vertical = "upwind"). The FV3 sweeps are transposed at the limiter branches of the recorded state; see the adjoint of the FV3 vertical sweep

The split-sweep PPMScheme with the FV3 vertical profile has no adjoint; neither do limited SlopesScheme and NoAdvection. require_adjoint_support(scheme) returns a supported scheme and otherwise throws an error that names the missing piece. The inversion driver applies it to its [advection] table; a Lin–Rood table without vertical selects fv3_kord8 there as in forward runs.

The supporting kernel adjoints in src/Operators/Advection/linrood_adjoint_*.jl are transposition-tested (test/core/test_linrood_kernel_adjoints.jl) and finite-difference VJP-tested via single-panel and cross-panel halo compositions. The full LinRood footprint, including its two Upwind Z half-sweeps, matches central differences to about 1e-11 relative on a smooth base field. test/core/test_cs_linrood_fv3_adjoint.jl asserts 1e-9 with upward vertical flux and a surface-layer objective, the case most sensitive to which air mass the Z records hold. Every tape records the air mass entering a Z sweep, because the upwind adjoint coefficient F / m_donor uses the pre-sweep donor mass; the FV3 profile's records also hold the tracer mass entering the sweep. test/core/test_cs_linrood_fv3_adjoint.jl checks the FV3 vertical sweeps' transpose in 256-bit arithmetic and the Lin–Rood footprints with them against central differences (1e-9, upward and downward flux, ORD 5 and 7, both profiles), and Full/Stride/Revolve parity.

The opt-in test/diagnostic/test_cs_transport_adjoint_gpu.jl also exercises transporting PPM and LinRood footprints on CUDA with scalar indexing disabled. It checks Float32/Float64 CPU/GPU agreement, Float64 directional finite differences, and full/stride/revolve checkpoint parity, plus the single-panel recording and reverse wrappers. LinRood copy-back and halo-gradient updates run on the array backend; the tape path does not require host scalar reads.

The CS reverse pass also supports the default, unclamped/full-column/unmerged forms of TM5Convection, CMFMCConvection, and CMFMCMatrixConvection. CMFMC and CMFMC-matrix have column adjoint-identity tests; the TM5/CMFMC footprint paths are checked against finite-difference emission gradients in test_cs_ppm_adjoint_footprint.jl.

The step plan: the adjoint replays production ​

The forward model the reverse pass transposes is the production step by construction (owner decision D31). A StepPlan (Operators/StepPlan) describes a run's step in four phases — window advance, window start, every step, window end — with the physics cadence, the binary window contract and the air-mass reset mode resolved once. TransportModel.step! and DrivenSimulation execute it; the adjoint replays the same plan with the production operators on a single-tracer state (CSStepSchedule; for a driven run CSStepSchedule(sim)) and records its tape through the recorder hooks of the production step (AbstractStepRecorder; production passes NoStepRecorder(), whose hooks are no-ops). Consequences:

  • physics_cadence = :window (the driven-run default under a binary window contract): convection is recorded once per met window, after the window's last step and the air-mass reset to the window's end mass, over the window length, with the window's forcing and (CMFMC) the CFL sub-step count of the forward call. Formerly the adjoint applied convection every step (finding OF-114).

  • A configuration without surface sources has the center V(Δt); footprints and 4D-Var always carry a surface-flux operator (zero rates allowed), and cs_surface_emission_footprint_from_seed(...; surface_flux = false) gives the initial-condition sensitivity of a no-emission run (initial_adjoint). Formerly the replay always built the coupled center V(Δt/2)SV(Δt/2) (finding OF-115).

  • The replay carries production's persistent operator state (the Kahan compensation of the surface source, the convection and Kz/Dkg diffusion ledger carries, the CMFMC CFL cache), and checkpoints save it, so the forward replay, the tape recording and every checkpoint restart equal the production run bit for bit.

  • require_adjoint_support(plan, ops) (also require_adjoint_support(sim)) rejects, before recording, every stage or operator without a record and an adjoint (adjoint_support(x) is the trait), naming it.

  • cs_adjoint_inputs(sim; tracer) captures the adjoint's inputs from a production DrivenSimulation (per-step face fluxes as production refreshes them, per-window convection forcing, diffusion layer thickness and Kz, emission rates, the schedule, fresh workspaces). Capture rejects initial nonzero compensation or carries and valid CMFMC CFL caches, including models continued across binaries at iteration zero. CSStepSchedule(sim) validates the production operators and retains chemistry. Reset windows and targets use the model backend. Diffusion records carry the forward's clock, so time-varying Kz fields are transposed at the times production evaluated them.

test/core/test_cs_adjoint_step_plan_parity.jl is the parity matrix: Upwind, unlimited slopes, monotone PPM and Lin–Rood (plus CW84 PPM, unlimited PPM and Lin–Rood ORD 5 with upwind vertical) under :window and :substep cadence, with and without the binary window contract, TM5, CMFMC and CMFMC-matrix convection, both diffusion couplings, diffusion without surface sources and both reset modes. Each case compares the forward replay, the tape recording and a restart from a checkpoint inside a met window with the production DrivenSimulation (== in one thread), Full/Stride/Revolve footprints with each other, and, on a subset, footprints and the initial-condition sensitivity with central differences of the production simulation (Upwind ∼10−14, monotone PPM 4×10−12, Lin–Rood 5×10−11 relative).

Checkpoint schedules ​

src/Tape/CheckpointSchedule.jl ships three checkpoint policies, selectable via the checkpoint kwarg of cs_surface_emission_footprint, cs_surface_emission_footprint_from_seed, cs_surface_flux_jacobian and cs_surface_flux_4dvar:

PolicyMemoryRecompute
FullCheckpointO(N) state snapshotsnone — fastest reverse pass
StrideCheckpoint(stride)O(N/stride)replays each stride forward
RevolveCheckpoint()O(log N)recursive bisection; each step may be replayed once per recursion level

RevolveCheckpoint() has no snapshot-budget argument. It is a recursive bisection variant rather than the optimal binomial Revolve: peak snapshots are proportional to the recursion depth and total replay work is O(N log N). It is covered in test/core/test_cs_stride_checkpoint.jl. All three schedules share one driver per policy for every scheme family; a checkpoint is a replay snapshot (tracer and air mass with halos plus the persistent operator state), so a restart inside a met window runs that window's remaining steps and window-end stages exactly as the recording run.

Tape storage backends ​

Split-sweep tape records can live on the device (the default), in pinned-host memory, or on disk via mmap — selectable via the tape_storage kwarg (:device / :pinned_host / :mmap). Storage backends are defined in src/Tape/TapeStorage.jl and src/Tape/MmapTapeStorage.jl; the mmap path is covered by test_cs_tape_mmap_roundtrip.jl. LinRood tape records currently require :device storage.

Inversion scaffold ​

src/Adjoints/Inversion/ ships:

ModuleSurface
Covariance.jlDiagonalCSCovariance, IsotropicGaussianCSCovariance, apply_B_half!, apply_B_half_adjoint!
Preconditioning.jlapply_preconditioner!, LinearOptimType, LogNormalOptimType
Optimizer.jlAbstractCSOptimizer, CSGradientDescent, CSLBFGS (via multiple-dispatch surfaces)
Jacobian.jlFootprint-Jacobian assembly for batched observation operators
CostGradient.jl4D-Var cost / gradient evaluator with preconditioning
Observations.jl, ObservationColumns.jl, ObservationBinding.jl, ObservationsIO.jlTyped observation surface (time sampling, placed point objectives, column meteorology, stencils) + on-disk schema v2
DeparturesIO.jlDepartures-file IO

These are all on CI. Full inversion tests: test_cs_4dvar_single_sweep.jl, test_cs_4dvar_placed_observations.jl, test_cs_gradient_checks.jl, test_cs_lbfgs.jl, test_cs_inversion_driver.jl, test_cs_inversion_truth_recovery.jl, test_cs_iteration_log.jl, test_cs_observations_io.jl, test_cs_observation_binding.jl, test_cs_departures_io.jl, test_cs_covariance.jl, test_cs_preconditioning.jl, test_cs_optimizer_dispatch.jl.

Single-sweep 4D-Var gradient ​

cs_surface_flux_4dvar computes the observation term of the cost and its gradient with one taped forward run and one reverse pass, whatever the number of observations, as TM5-4DVAR does.

Observations as linear functionals. An observation i is sampled after the model steps s∈Si of its time sampling (one step, or the steps of a time window with weights ωis summing to 1; see observation operators), after convection: the state runtime output and the forward observation sampler see. The meteorology is fixed, so the air mass m of every step is known before any tracer is transported, and the observation operator is a fixed sparse linear functional of the tracer masses rs at those steps,

Hi(x)=ci+∑s∈Siωis∑ewisers[e],

with weights from the replayed air mass at each s: w=1/max(m,ϵ) on one cell for CSLayerMeanObjective and for the layer a CSPlacedPointObjective reads at that step (ϵ the machine epsilon, the floor of its evaluation), w=1/∑kmk on every level of a column for CSColumnMeanObjective, and ci=0; an averaging-kernel column (CSRetrievalColumnObjective) has wk=Hk/max(mk,ϵ) on every level and its prior term as the offset ci (averaging-kernel columns). Its gradient ∂Hi/∂rs is ωiswis. An instantaneous observation (one step, ω=1) gives exactly the functional it had before time windows existed.

One reverse sweep. Write Ms for the tangent-linear model of step s (the transport palindrome with the surface-flux center, then convection) and λs for the adjoint state at the end of step s. The cost Jobs=12∑i((Hi(x)−yi)/σi)2 has the gradient of a sum, so all observations share one recursion,

λN=fN,λs=Ms+1Tλs+1+fs,fs=∑i:s∈SiHi(x)−yiσi2ωiswis,

run from the last sampled step N back to the first step. Every recorder ends each step with an end-of-step marker (_CSStepEndRecord, after the convection record); the reverse walk adds fs there, before it transposes that step's convection. This is the TM5-4DVAR structure: its forcing enters just before the adjoint of the operator after which the forward run sampled. Where the walk reaches the midpoint of step t (the palindrome center, where the step's surface emissions enter) it reads Δtλ as ∂Jobs/∂Et, and each control window sums its steps.

The forcing entries are grouped by step, panel and cell; the injection kernel gives each cell one work item, which adds the cell's entries in input order, so the injection is deterministic without atomics. With FullCheckpoint one evaluation therefore costs a forward run for H(x) and the weights, one taped forward run to the last observation step, and one reverse pass; StrideCheckpoint adds its checkpoint propagation pass and RevolveCheckpoint its O(log⁡N) recomputation, as for a footprint. Steps after the last observation do not affect the cost and get a zero gradient. checkpoint, tape_storage and tape_path choose how that one taped run is stored. test/core/test_cs_4dvar_single_sweep.jl checks the gradient against one footprint per observation (the previous algorithm, rebuilt in the test) for upwind, unlimited slopes and PPM, monotone PPM and Lin–Rood with diffusion of both surface-flux couplings, TM5 and CMFMC convection and the three checkpoint schedules, and for CW84-limited PPM and Lin–Rood with the FV3 vertical sweep (10−12 relative in Float64, 10−5 in Float32), and counts tape reads to confirm one recording and one reverse pass per gradient.

cs_surface_flux_jacobian likewise records its tape once and walks it once per objective (with FullCheckpoint); each walk is the one a separate cs_surface_emission_footprint call makes.

Observation operators: point samples in the column and time windows ​

Observation files use schema v2 (schemas/cs_observations_v2.toml): Float64 coordinates, a kind ("point" for an in-situ sample, "column" for a column average), the vertical fields elevation_m, intake_height_m, altitude_m and pressure_pa (NaN when a record does not give them), a time_window_s, a quality flag and a model_sigma. bind_to_mesh turns each record into a CSObservation; its sigma is σ=(σobs2+σmod2)1/2.

Cell. The record binds to the cell that contains its point (the grid-box stencil), found with the forward observation sampler's locator, so a record is sampled and inverted in the same cell. Float32 coordinates (schema v1) could put a point within rounding of a cell edge into the neighbouring cell; v1 files are rejected.

Vertical placement. A point record becomes a CSPlacedPointObjective, placed once by the forward sampler's rule (Observations.resolve_placement) with the vertical_coordinates of the placement settings, in preference order (default height above ground, then pressure):

  • by its height above the true ground h: intake_height_m, else altitude_m − elevation_m, else altitude_m minus a DEM elevation at the point. h is measured up from the model surface, whatever the model surface height: the model ground lies above or below the true ground, and a mountain station belongs in the model's lowest layers, not at its absolute altitude. Absolute altitudes are an explicit option (absolute_altitude_above_agl_m);

  • by its pressure pobs (a total pressure).

A point record that gives none of the coordinates in use is unplaced: an error, or dropped and counted with unplaced_records = "skip". A column record without a retrieval block becomes a CSColumnMeanObjective; one with a block becomes an averaging-kernel column.

The layer is chosen at every sampled state s from that state's replayed dry air mass mk (kg per cell, k=1 at the top) and the column meteorology (CSObservationColumnMet: model-top pressure ptop, gravity g, layer temperature Tk, specific humidity qk), with the forward sampler's function Observations.sample_column_layer!. With the cell area A, the total interface pressures (from the dry air mass and the humidity) and the hypsometric interface heights above the model surface are

p1/2=ptop,pk+1/2=pk−1/2+gmkA(1−qk),zN+1/2=0,zk−1/2=zk+1/2+RdTk(1+cqk)gln⁡pk+1/2pk−1/2,

with the virtual temperature Tk(1+cqk), c=Rv/Rd−1 (VIRTUAL_TEMPERATURE_FACTOR, 0.61) (pressure_basis = "total", the default). With pressure_basis = "dry", for meteorology without humidity, both are built from the dry interfaces pk+1/2d=pk−1/2d+gmk/A and Tk: an approximation whose heights are about 2 % low in a humid boundary layer (finding OF-117). A record placed by height reads the layer with zk+1/2≤h<zk−1/2 (the lowest layer for h≤0); a record placed by pressure reads the layer with pk−1/2≤pobs<pk+1/2 of the same basis. The sampled value is the dry mixing ratio of that layer, hs=rs,ks/max(ms,ks,ϵ). The layer depends only on the meteorology, not on the tracer, so it is fixed in an evaluation and the functional weight 1/max(ms,ks,ϵ) is the exact derivative of the evaluated value: every vertical coordinate enters the adjoint by construction.

Time sampling. Step s covers Is=[t0+(s−1)Δt,t0+sΔt) and is represented by the state at its end. A record without a window samples the step whose interval contains its time t (ω=1). A record with a window W>0 samples

ωs=|Is∩[t−W/2,t+W/2]∩[t0,t0+NΔt)|∑s′|Is′∩[t−W/2,t+W/2]∩[t0,t0+NΔt)|,H=∑sωshs:

steps fully inside the window weigh Δt, a step partly inside weighs its overlap, and the window is truncated at the run's ends and renormalised. A window narrower than a step inside one interval is the instantaneous sample. Whether a record is in the run is decided by its time t (out_of_range_policy); ClampOutOfRange keeps a record outside the run: the part of its window inside the run, truncated and renormalised, or the first or last step when it has no window or the window misses the run (departure rows mark such records clamped). Window records need the run length (nsteps), which bounds their steps.

This time sampling differs from the forward observation sampler's: the sampler takes its samples at met-window ends (a linear blend of the two ends around the record time, or the nearest end), while the inversion takes the state at the end of the model step containing the record time (up to one step Δt after it) or the Δt-weighted mean over its window. Both place a sample in the same layer of the same state and read the same value there; for an arbitrary record time they sample different states.

CS4DVarResult.stencils returns, per observation, the cell, the sampled steps and weights, the level read at each step, the placement code and the height or pressure that placed it; build_departure_set joins them to the records (by id) in schema-v2 departure files (schemas/cs_departures_v2.toml).

Relation to TM5-4DVAR. Matched: the sample is taken right after a fixed operator (here the end of the step, after convection) and its forcing enters just before that operator's transpose, in one reverse sweep; windows are Δt/ΣΔt means with weights fixed at binding; the horizontal stencil is fixed per observation (TM5 also offers slopes and trilinear stencils; ours is the grid box, a type that can gain a trilinear form for both the sampler and the inversion); the vertical stencil is chosen from the same meteorology forward and in reverse. Different: points are placed by their height above the true ground measured from the model surface (TM5 compares sea-level altitudes with heights on the model orography and never samples layer 1); pressure placement is in the adjoint too (TM5's adjoint uses the altitude only, so its gradient of pressure-coordinate points is wrong); a step partly inside a window counts its overlap (TM5 counts the half steps fully inside); the basis is dry; and records carry their flag, elevation, intake height and pressure.

test/core/test_cs_4dvar_placed_observations.jl checks parity with the forward sampler on one state (same layer and value through build_observation_sampler in nearest-window mode, records sampled at the window end that closes their model step, and through bind_to_mesh + cs_surface_flux_4dvar), a 10 m intake against a 5 km aircraft sample, total against dry pressure placement, layers that follow the replayed air mass step by step, a window observation's value and gradient against the Δt-weighted sum of its single-step observations (10−12), the single sweep against per-observation footprints for placed and window observations (10−12, upwind, monotone PPM and Lin–Rood, TM5 convection, Full and Stride checkpoints), and central finite differences of the cost.

Averaging-kernel columns ​

A retrieved column-averaged dry mole fraction (OCO-2, GOSAT, TROPOMI, TCCON) is not the column mean of the true profile: the retrieval weights the atmosphere with its averaging kernel and fills in its prior where it has little sensitivity. A column record that carries a retrieval block (schema v2, schemas/cs_observations_v2.toml) is compared with the model through that retrieval's own vertical description, with the operator of TM5-4DVAR (deps/tm5-cy3-4dvar/base/f2py/src/averaging_kernels.F90, the OCO-2 routine applyaveragingkernel and the rebin inv_rebin). A block describes either layer means (retrieval_mapping = "layer_rebin", this section) or values on levels with the profile linear between them ("hat_levels", the OCO-2/OCO-3 retrievals; see level retrievals). A layer block gives the retrieval's N layers from the surface up:

  • interfaces p1r>p2r>⋯>pN+1r≥0 (Pa, total pressure), with p1r=psr the retrieval surface pressure and pN+1r=ptr its top;

  • pressure weights hi≥0 with ∑ihi=1 (checked to 10−4: a deficit δ would bias the column by δX);

  • the column averaging kernel ai, normalized, so that ∂X/∂xi=hiai on the retrieval layers;

  • the prior profile xa,i (dry mole fraction, mol mol⁻¹; files state the unit, ppm and ppb are converted). The operator adds it to the model's dry mole fractions, so the record value and errors and the transported tracer are in mol mol⁻¹ too: such a file states a mole-fraction unit on value, value_sigma and model_sigma (converted to mol mol⁻¹), and a record must be an absolute column average, a value in (0, 1] with errors not above it;

  • optionally retrieval_profile_sigma, an uncertainty σi of the model profile on the retrieval layers (mol mol⁻¹), for the model-error term below.

bind_to_mesh turns such a record into a CSRetrievalColumnObjective. At every sampled state the model's interface pressures pk+1/2 of its cell are built as for pressure placement: total pressures from the replayed dry air mass and the specific humidity, pk+1/2=pk−1/2+gmk/(A(1−qk)) (pressure_basis = "total", the default; retrieval pressures are total pressures), or the dry interfaces ("dry"). Model surface and top are ps=pNz+1/2 and pt=p1/2. Then (Observations.retrieval_column_weights!):

  1. Stretch. The model interfaces are mapped linearly onto the retrieval's pressure range, the model surface onto the retrieval surface and the model top onto the retrieval top:
sk+1/2=μpk+1/2+c,μ=psr−ptrps−pt,c=12[(psr−μps)+(ptr−μpt)].
  1. Rebin. Each retrieval layer takes the pressure-weighted mean of the stretched model layers it overlaps:
Rik=|[sk−1/2,sk+1/2]∩[pi+1r,pir]|pir−pi+1r,(Rx)i=∑kRikxk,

with the outermost retrieval interfaces taken from the stretched model column (TM5's choice; they equal psr and ptr to rounding). Every row of R sums to 1 and ∑iRik(pir−pi+1r)=sk+1/2−sk−1/2: the rebin conserves the column integral.

  1. Column.
X=∑ihiai(Rx)i+∑ihi(1−ai)xa,i=∑kHkxk+c,Hk=∑ihiaiRik,

on the model's dry mixing ratios xk=rk/max(mk,ϵ).

The pressures depend on the meteorology only, so X is linear in the tracer mass with weights wk=Hk/max(mk,ϵ) on every level of the cell and the offset c (_linear_functional is the exact derivative of the evaluation; a window record takes the ωs-weighted sum over its steps, each step with its own pressures). The adjoint forcing is TM5's per-layer H⋅(X−y)/σ2.

What the stretch does physically. The stretch keeps every model layer's share of the column, (sk+1/2−sk−1/2)/(psr−ptr)=(pk+1/2−pk−1/2)/(ps−pt): it moves the model column onto the retrieval's pressure range without adding or removing air, and it absorbs both a surface-pressure mismatch Δps=ps−psr and a different top. With a=1 and weights normalized to the retrieval column the operator returns the model's pressure-weighted column mean for any Δps. A mismatch changes only where the model's layers sit against the vertical structure of the kernel. Where the model surface lies below the sounding's true ground (Δps>0, smoothed model orography under a mountain sounding), the model's boundary layer is compressed onto the retrieval's lowest layers instead of being cut off below the retrieval surface, which would remove boundary-layer air, and its enhancements, from the column; a 30 hPa mismatch moves every interface by about 3 % of its pressure. This is why the default is no limit, as in TM5. The same holds at the top: when the retrieval top lies well below the model top (a retrieval grid that stops at 10 hPa, say), the stretch packs the whole model column, stratosphere included, into the retrieval's pressure range, as TM5 does, so X is a full-column mean of the model, not a partial column above the retrieval top.

Surface-pressure mismatch policy. max_surface_pressure_mismatch_pa (bind_to_mesh keyword; [observations.placement] key of the inversion driver; default no limit) bounds |Δps|, the time-weighted model minus retrieval surface pressure over the sampled steps, with the model surface pressure of the stretch's pressure basis (with "dry", Δps also contains the vapour weight, about 0.5 % of the surface pressure). A record above the limit follows the unplaced policy: with unplaced_records = "error" (default) the 4D-Var stops and names the records; with "skip" the record is reported (simulated value, residual, its stencil with assimilated = false) but adds nothing to the cost or the gradient, and the number of such records is logged. The model surface pressure is known only at the sampled states, so the check runs in the 4D-Var's forward replay; it depends on the meteorology only, so the same records are left out in every iteration.

Model-error term. When the record gives a model-profile uncertainty σi (retrieval_profile_sigma), the observation error is σ2=σobs2+σmod2+∑i(hiaiσi)2 (Observations.retrieval_model_error_variance): the operator's weights on the retrieval layers, squared, times the profile variance, the layers taken independent. It depends on the record only, not on the state or the meteorology, so it is fixed when the record is bound and the cost stays quadratic in every iteration (TM5 freezes its σmod at the first iteration for the same reason). It is analogous to, not the same as, TM5's term: TM5's CH4 TROPOMI routine (averaging_kernels.F90, line 669) evaluates ∑kHk2σk2 with the weights H=(ha)R on the model layers and the spread of the modelled profiles, and its OCO-2 routine adds a column model error instead. The input is an uncertainty of the model profile (representation or transport error). Do not pass the retrieval's a-priori uncertainty: the smoothing error it causes is already represented by the averaging kernel.

Diagnostics. The stencil of an averaging-kernel column (CSObservationStencil, placement code RETRIEVAL_COLUMN_PLACEMENT_CODE = −3, level 0) carries Δps, the model profile on the retrieval layers Rx (time-weighted) and assimilated; departure files add them with the profile model sigma (schemas/cs_departures_v2.toml).

Relation to TM5-4DVAR. Matched: the stretch (including its averaging of the two offsets), the overlap matrix of inv_rebin with its outer interfaces, the column and its per-layer forcing; the test reproduces values computed with TM5's Fortran on fixed columns to 10−14 (the stretched interfaces exactly; H can differ in the last bit from the Fortran's matmul summation order). Different:

  • the operator is in the model, a linear functional of the tracer mass at each sampled step (a window record averages the operator over its steps), where TM5 writes the Δt-averaged profile and surface pressure to a track file and applies the kernel once in Python;

  • dry basis: x is the dry mixing ratio and the interfaces are total pressures rebuilt from the dry air mass and the humidity; TM5 uses moist rm/m and AT+BTps of its moist surface pressure;

  • the pressure weights come from the record and must sum to 1; TM5's OCO-2 routine computes hi=Δpi/psr, which leaves out the column above a retrieval top above 0 Pa;

  • an explicit mismatch policy, where TM5's OCO-2 path has none and its CH4 TROPOMI path sets a huge σ above a tolerance (the same effect as "skip");

  • a rebin that fails TM5's checks (possible only for a retrieval layer thinner than the stretch's rounding) is an error, not a silent zero departure;

  • the model-profile uncertainty is given on the retrieval layers by the record; TM5's CH4 TROPOMI path uses the spread of the modelled profile on model layers from its track file.

test/core/test_cs_4dvar_retrieval_columns.jl checks agreement with TM5's Fortran (reference values computed with averaging_kernels.F90 itself, with the model surface below and above the retrieval's and the retrieval top above and below the model top) and with a line-by-line transcription on random columns, conservation by the rebin, the pressure-weighted and air-mass-weighted column means for a=1 on the model's levels, the schema block (units, ordering, NaN padding, errors), the single sweep against a seeded footprint per observation and step (10−12; upwind, monotone PPM, Lin–Rood, TM5 convection, Full and Stride checkpoints), central finite differences with window records, the mismatch policy, and the departure diagnostics.

Level retrievals (OCO-2, OCO-3): the hat projection ​

The OCO-2 and OCO-3 retrievals (Lite files and the v11 MIP 10-second files) give their prior and column averaging kernel on 20 levels, σj=pj/ps from 10−4 (top) to 1 (surface), "defined on layer boundaries": the retrieval's state vector holds the profile at the levels and the profile is linear in pressure between them. Their pressure weights are the integrals of the levels' hat functions φj (φj(pj)=1, falling linearly to 0 at the neighbouring levels): the trapezoid rule, half-thickness end levels, with a dry-air correction. A record whose block has retrieval_mapping = "hat_levels" (Observations.HatLevelProjection) stores the 20 level pressures, weights hj, kernel aj and prior xa,j surface first, and the model column is projected onto the hats.

Projection. The model interfaces are stretched as for layer retrievals, the model surface onto the bottom level and the model top onto the top level (sk±1/2, each layer keeping its share of the column). The level values cj of the model profile are its L2 (Galerkin) projection onto the hats in dry air: the piecewise-linear profile ∑jcjφj closest to the model profile, weighted by dry air,

∑iMjici=bj,Mji=∫φjφidpdry,bj=∫φjxdpdry=∑kBjkxk,Bjk=mksk+1/2−sk−1/2∫sk−1/2sk+1/2φj(p)dp,

each stretched layer's dry air mk spread evenly over its pressure thickness; M is tridiagonal (neighbouring hats overlap), so P=M−1B costs one tridiagonal solve per column and step. The column is the operator of the layer case with P in place of the rebin R:

X=Xa+∑jhjaj(cj−xa,j)=∑kHkxk+c,H=(h∘a)TM−1B,

with h, a, xa and the prior column Xa from the file (the MIP protocol's eq. 2; the kernel is already normalized: it is not multiplied by h). Xa is the file's xco2_apriori, carried by the converter and the forward sampler's reader (retrieval_prior_column in observation files); a record without one uses Xa=∑jhjxa,j, the form of the layer case. The 10-s averages of the weights and of the prior were taken separately, so the two differ: by up to about 0.01 ppm (−0.012 ppm for sounding 20210804153946), a shift of every simulated column. X is still linear in the tracer: the 4D-Var functional is exact as before, with weights Hk/max(mk,ϵ) built from the replayed air mass and pressures of each sampled step.

Why the projection. The basis contains the constants (the hats sum to 1 over the stretched column), so the projection preserves the column integral: the rows of P sum to 1, and with the hat integrals of the model's dry air as weights, hjm=∑kBjk/∑kmk, the projected profile has the model's dry column mean exactly, ∑jhjmcj=∑kmkxk/∑kmk. The file's weights are the same integrals with the retrieval's own humidity, so the column is conserved with them to the difference of the two dry-air corrections. And a projection reproduces every profile its basis can represent: a model profile that is piecewise linear on the levels, the retrieval's own representation, gives its level values back exactly (to the discretization of the model's layer means, second order in the layer thickness), so the kernel is applied to the level values it was derived for. A model profile equal to the retrieval's prior gives the prior column, to the projection's discretization: on 960 OCO-2 records of 2019-07-01, with the prior sampled as the layer means of a fine column aligned with the levels (760 layers), X−Xa is −7e-6 ppm (5–95 %: −9e-6 to −4e-6). On a GEOS L72 column, whose layers do not line up with the levels, |X−Xa|=|∑jhjaj(cj−xa,j)| ranges from 1e-5 to 2.1e-3 ppm and single level values cj differ from xa,j by up to 0.57 ppm (independent review): the level values carry the model's coarse vertical sampling, the column much less. The hat average ∫φjx/∫φj (M lumped onto its diagonal), which is not a projection, puts that column −0.0185 ppm low (−0.021 to −0.012), because the prior is curved in the stratosphere; for a +10 ppm boundary layer below σ=0.95 it is 0.018 ppm below the projection. P, the inverse of the consistent mass matrix times B, has negative entries in general (about −0.21 to −0.23 in every row on a GEOS L72 column), which a linear operator allows; the column weights H stayed positive on OCO-2 records (on L72, minkHk was 0.23–0.39 of their mean).

The top level. The top level sits at σ=10−4 (10 Pa), not at

  1. The stretch maps the whole model column, from its top (about 1 Pa for

GEOS, 0 for ERA5) to its surface, onto [10−4ps,ps], every layer keeping its share, so nothing is cut off: the model stratosphere above 53 hPa falls under the top half-hat (h≈0.026) and the model's air above 10 Pa (10−4 of the column) is squeezed into it. The weights sum to 1 over the levels.

TM5-4DVAR's 19 layers. Observations.tm5_layer_column builds TM5-4DVAR's layer form of the same record (proj/tracer/CO2/py/Observations.py, 7016–7052; Satellite.py, 707–717): the 20 levels as the interfaces of 19 layers, the kernel and prior interpolated to the layer midpoints, the weights Δpi, then the layer operator (rebin R). TM5 divides the thicknesses by ps, so its weights sum to 1−10−4; this mode normalizes them to 1 (TM5's column is 0.9999 times this one). It is for comparisons with TM5-4DVAR co-samples (converter mapping = Observations.LayerRebin() or --mapping tm5, forward sampler averaging_kernel_mapping = "tm5"). For a +10 ppm boundary layer below σ=0.95 on the prior, the mode is 0.009 ppm above the hat projection (5–95 %: +0.002 to +0.017; 960 records of 2019-07-01).

The MIP point formula. The MIP protocol writes the column as X=Xprior+∑jhjaj(cj−cprior,j) with cj the model profile at the levels, without saying how to transform the model to them. Point values are not column-conserving: for a +10 ppm boundary layer below σ=0.95 (ΔX = +0.49 ppm) the point form is 0.232 ppm below the hat projection (5–95 %: 0.230–0.236 ppm; 960 records of 2019-07-01). At c=xa, TM5's unnormalized weights put its column 0.033 ppm below the point form. Neither point values nor boxes centred on the levels are offered.

Tests. test/core/test_retrieval_hat_projection.jl: the projection matrix against an independent construction (exact integration of the hats and their products), rows summing to 1, column conservation with the hat integrals, a piecewise-linear profile reproduced at every level, ends and kinks included, within Δmax|v′|/N2 for N layers per interval (second order), a model profile equal to the prior giving the prior column within 1e-5 ppm (synthetic and real MIP records), TM5 mode against a transcription of TM5's Python, level records in schema v2. test/core/test_cs_4dvar_oco2_mip.jl: the single sweep against a seeded footprint per observation and step for level columns, windows and TM5-mode records (10−12, upwind and monotone PPM), and central finite differences.

OCO-2 MIP records: converter, co-sampling, cell averages ​

Converter. read_oco2_mip_observations(path; ...) reads an OCO-2 or OCO-3 v11 MIP 10-second file (OCO2_b11.2_10sec_GOOD_r2/r3.nc4, OCO3_b11_10sec_GOOD_r2.nc4) into schema-v2 column records with a level block, and convert_oco2_mip_observations(path, output; partition = :day) writes one file per day ({YYYYMMDD}) or month ({YYYYMM}):

bash
julia --project=. scripts/preprocessing/oco2_mip_to_observations.jl \
    OCO2_b11.2_10sec_GOOD_r2.nc4 'obs/oco2_mip_{YYYYMMDD}.nc' \
    --start 2019-01-01 --stop 2019-02-01 --data-types LN,LG,OG --assimilate-flags 1

sounding_id → id; date[1:6] → date_components (truncated to the second, as TM5 reads it); latitude, longitude; kind = "column"; altitude → elevation_m; time_window_s = 0; xco2_2019_scale, xco2_uncertainty and model_error (or a constant, --model-sigma) → value, value_sigma, model_sigma (ppm → mol/mol); the levels (σ⋅ps, hPa → Pa), weights, kernel and prior (ppm → mol/mol), turned surface first, and the prior column xco2_apriori. Every record of the time range is written: flag = 0 when its assimilate_flag is in the experiment's set (--assimilate-flags, 1 by default) and its data type too (--data-types: LN, LG, OG by default; SAM names OCO-3's snapshot area maps, data_type = 0), else flag = 1 + assimilate_flag (1 evaluation-only scenes, 2 assimilable but outside the data types, 3 withheld). instrument_type is <instrument>_<data type> (OCO2_OG); the files record the source file, the options and the mapping as root attributes. OCO-2 and OCO-3 sounding ids can coincide, so keep the instruments in separate sets.

Forward-only co-sampling. The MIP needs co-samples of every record, withheld and evaluation-only ones included. bind_to_mesh(...; flagged_records = "cosample") (CosampleFlaggedRecords; the inversion driver's [observations].flagged_records) binds records with a nonzero flag as co-samples, CSObservation(...; assimilate = false): the forward replay simulates them, CS4DVarResult reports their simulated values, residuals and stencils (assimilated = false), but they add nothing to the cost or the gradient, are not screened by the surface-pressure limit, and do not extend the taped run: the cost is bit for bit that without them, and the reverse pass receives bit-identical forcing and tape length (the gradient is bit for bit that without them single-threaded; with several threads the adjoint kernels are not bit-reproducible from one call to the next, at about 10−22 of the largest entry, with or without co-samples). Departure files carry each row's flag (build_departure_set), so one file holds the co-samples of all records. The default ("drop") is unchanged.

Cell averages. About 59 % of the assimilated OCO-2 10-s records share a C90 cell with another record of the same orbit (1.43 per orbit and cell, about 9 s apart). cell_averaging = CellAverage(; time_tolerance_s = 60, correlation = 0) ([observations.cell_averaging], mode = "average") averages the assimilated column records of one tracer, cell and step sampling that lie within time_tolerance_s of the earliest record of their group. With wi=1/σi2 (value_sigma):

y¯=∑iwiyi∑iwi,H¯=∑iwiHi∑iwi,σmeas2=∑i∑jwiwjρijσiσj(∑iwi)2,σ¯2=σmeas2+∑iwiσmod,i2∑iwi,

ρii=1 and ρij= correlation between distinct spans (0: the within-span correlation is already in σi); the model error (model_sigma and the profile term) is added once, not reduced. H¯ is a CSCellAverageObjective, exact for the linear operators: its gradient is the w-weighted combination of the members'. The members stay as co-samples, so departures keep one row per record, with the average's cell_average_id, and the average is a row of its own, the term of the cost (placement code −4, cell_average_id its number 1, 2, …, a row id above every record id of the observation set, y¯, H¯x, σmeas in value_sigma, the model error in model_sigma, ρ in cell_average_correlation): over the assimilated rows, ∑ normalized_departure² =2Jobs. Averaging needs max_surface_pressure_mismatch_pa = Inf (a CSCellAverageObjective built by hand is checked the same way). The alternative, inflate_cell_model_error(set, mesh, t_start, dt; ...) (mode = "inflate_model_error"), keeps the records and multiplies each record's model_sigma² by the number k of records of its group; the profile-error term of an averaging-kernel column is not inflated.

Forward sampler. An oco2_lite source of [output.observations] with averaging_kernel_tracers = ["co2"] (opt-in) also reads each sounding's retrieval (Observations.read_oco2_retrieval_columns) and writes co2_ak_column, the same operator (averaging_kernel_mapping = "hat" or "tm5") on the sampled profile and the interface pressures of pressure_basis. Without the key the output is unchanged. The test checks that, in nearest-window mode, the sampler's value equals the 4D-Var's simulated value of the same record converted to schema v2 (10−13), and that the default sounding file is identical.

What is not yet shipped ​

ItemNotes
Optimal binomial RevolveRevolveCheckpoint ships as the bisection variant — logarithmic memory but not the Griewank–Walther optimal recompute count. Optimal binomial Revolve is the next refinement.
Optimized/clamped convection adjointsCMFMC clamp = true and TM5/CMFMC-matrix collaborative, truncated, or merged solves are rejected by the footprint API until their exact branches are taped and transposed.
TM5-4DVAR cross-validationSynthetic truth-recovery via test_cs_inversion_truth_recovery.jl is on CI; a side-by-side parity run against TM5-4DVAR on real data has not been published.
Inversion driver on transport binariesscripts/inversions/cs_4dvar.jl binds observation files only on its synthetic meteorology (synthetic_hydrostatic); a 4D-Var on transport-binary meteorology is assembled with the Julia API (bind_to_mesh, CSObservationColumnMet, cs_surface_flux_4dvar).
Tangent-linear modelForward TL is not exposed as a separate driver. If you need it, use the reverse pass plus identity seeding.

Adjoint-readiness in the forward design ​

Three concrete forward-design choices that pay off in the adjoint:

  • Vertical diffusion — generic Kz kernels expose the tridiagonal coefficients (a, b, c) and transpose the backward-Euler solve with its mass/VMR scaling. The precomputed Dkg mass path exposes the retention fractions of two conservative bidiagonal solves. Its reverse applies those passes' transposes in reverse order, preserving a constant total-mass gradient exactly for positive carrier masses.

  • Convection (CMFMC + TM5) — apply! takes a ConvectionForcing carrier explicitly so the operator does not call current_time internally; this keeps the operator pure-functional in the time variable. The TM5 reverse pass rebuilds the same per-column matrix and solves with the transposed LU factors.

  • Advection — the adjoint composes each operator's transpose in reverse order. The palindrome helps organize that reversal, but forward transport is not its own inverse. Stored states supply the limiter branches and reconstructed-face sensitivities needed by the reverse pass.

How to use the adjoint today ​

The maintained command-line path is the inversion driver:

bash
julia --project=. scripts/inversions/cs_4dvar.jl \
    config/inversions/example_synthetic.toml

That synthetic-only configuration owns observations, controls, covariance and optimizer choices, and an [advection] table that is parsed like a forward run's (limiter = "none", the unlimited PPM, is accepted only here). Unknown tables and keys are errors. [observations] takes inline entries or a schema-v2 observation file, whose point records [observations.placement] places in the column of the synthetic_hydrostatic meteorology (the keys of [output.observations] placement, parsed by the same code). It does not expose checkpoint, diffusion, convection or real-binary settings. For the lower-level Julia API, start with the footprint tutorial, then test/core/test_cs_inversion_truth_recovery.jl for a larger inversion assembly. Use RevolveCheckpoint() (without arguments) for recursive bisection, or StrideCheckpoint(K) for an explicit interval. LinRood checkpoints currently require tape_storage = :device; split-sweep schemes also support :pinned_host and :mmap.
